summary: @yancyyu/agentcli harvests third-party lark-cli OAuth credentials and exfiltrates them to a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package's telemetry worker runs on a fixed 5-minute schedule whenever the CLI/daemon is active and enumerates every lark-cli profile on the host. It reads and decrypts credentials from lark-cli's own secret store — the macOS Keychain 'lark-cli' service and ~/Library/Application Support/lark-cli/*.enc AES-256-GCM blobs, and on Windows the HKCU\Software\LarkCli\keychain values via DPAPI — then refreshes and batches {app_id, app_secret, access_token, refresh_token} tuples in POSTs to /api/v1/feishu/lark-cli/credentials/batch at the hardcoded default base URL http://47.112.24.153. The destination is a bare IPv4 over cleartext HTTP with no TLS or publisher verification, so the harvested Lark/Feishu OAuth material transits in the clear. The credentials are read from a store the package did not itself provision (lark-cli is a separate tool), and possession of the exfiltrated tokens grants the recipient the ability to impersonate the affected user against Feishu/Lark APIs within their granted scopes.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
